content:
I guided Claude and Codex to create lean-inductive-models.

This program is a lean-export-filter that adds, for every inductive (except the “basis” Eq Nat PUnit PSigma' Quot), a model of that inductive. A model comprises of definitions for the type itself, its constructor, its recursors and (if applicable) its projections, together with theorems for all the reduction rules, unit-like properties and eta rules. It liberally uses the standard axioms in its constructions.

It can also run in a no-output only checking mode, making it an external checker that adds additional strong guardrails to an existing checker: I believe that this protects against implementation bugs in the handling of inductive declarations, including the recent soundness bug about phantom parameters in nested declarations.

It can also be very useful for people who want to write or verify a new checker: By using this as a preprocessor, your checker may not have to fully check inductive declarations, it only has to check that they are justified by the model. (This is a weak ad-hoc form of extensional type theory, so meta-theoretical caveats apply. For risks and side effects consult your local type theorist).

It already runs as a checker on the Kernel Areana.

Congratulations!
This had been a long-standing TODO item in @Mario Carneiro 's paper.
Is it? Note that this is building a model for a concrete inductive, it is not a proof that every inductive has a model. (The difference between a verified compiler and a certifying compiler)
OK, but I believe that this is the significant step to prove it!
Maybe… I don’t expect that anything I did here is news or even helpful to Mario’s work, but happy to be proven wrong :-)

I DMed @Joachim Breitner these questions:

  • I think the idea here is that types like inductives (both nested and non nested) inductives can be represented via simpler types and this is converting the exported proofs to those simpler types, right?
  • is this conversion something that could be done at scale in practice, like convert all of mathlib’s export?
  • I’ve advocated for a while for a stopgap on Lean’s consistency proofs where while we wait for others to completely redesign Lean’s type theory to have nice metatheoretic properties, we find ways to finish a proof of the consistency of some practical kernel and put that in comparator. Could this be used for something like that?
  • would it be easier to complete lean4lean-model (the formal proof of LeanTT’s consistency) if it only covered the base objects you use here instead of all inductives. (I think @Kim Morrison has completed most of the proof already except for inductives and some quotient stuff, but maybe I’m mistaken.)
  • would it be easier to make a verified kernel (lean4lean style) of the fragment you need after running the export through this conversion? Is lean4lean almost there?

Here were @Joachim Breitner’s answers:

  • yes
  • Yes, and that already what's happening on the Kernel arena.
  • It could help to finish a consistency proof for a simpler checker that doesn't need to construct inductives
  • Yes, plausibly.
  • the third answer covers the last question as well
